finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar passes an attacker-supplied avatarUrl to axios.get. The only check is an https:// prefix, which does not constrain host, IP, port, or redirects. This allows blind SSRF to internal hosts and, via a redirect to plain http://169.254.169.254, cloud metadata. The response length is returned to the caller.
finding.source: server.js:10 req.body.avatarUrl (attacker-controlled JSON body, parsed at server.js:5)

trace.note: guard: typeof string and startsWith('https://'); scheme-only, no host/IP check
axios.get follows redirects by default, so the https check is not re-applied after a 3xx; no timeout or maxContentLength
returns img.data.length, leaking response size; the body is not returned

finding.guards_checked: server.js:11 typeof string and https:// prefix only. Not present: hostname/IP allowlist, private/loopback/link-local blocking, DNS rebinding protection, port restriction, redirect validation (maxRedirects:0), response size cap, timeout, auth middleware (none visible in this code). Express version unknown (no package.json), which affects whether upstream errors leak to the client.

verdict.guard_found: none closing. server.js:11 is only a typeof-string check plus a startsWith("https://") prefix check, which does not constrain host, IP, port, or redirects. No auth middleware, hostname allowlist, private-IP block, redirect limit, timeout, or size cap appears anywhere in server.js.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10, parsed by express.json at server.js:5) reaches axios.get at server.js:14 and the response length is returned at server.js:15; the only guard at server.js:11 is a scheme prefix, and axios follows redirects by default, so the finding stands.
